HI-2026-GM1366.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 15, 2026, the Governor signed the following bill into law: SB2338 SD1 HD2 CD1 (ACT 263).

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1366.aiSummary: Signed into law on July 15, 2026, this act changes pay rules for some Hawaii housing agencies. It lets the Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation and the Hawaii Community Development Authority set certain staff roles and salaries with fewer review steps, and it raises salary caps for the top leaders and one deputy role. It also sets rules for employment contracts at HHFDC, HCDA, and the Hawaii Public Housing Authority.

HI-2026-GM1360.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 15, 2026, the Governor returned the following bill with specific appropriation item(s) stricken or reduced: SB2600 SD1 HD1 CD1

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1360.policyArea: Line Item Veto of SB2600 SD1 HD1 CD1
HI-2026-GM1360.aiSummary: The governor returned SB 2600 with a line-item veto, which means he reduced one specific money item in the bill. The $50 million general fund deposit to the Emergency and Budget Reserve Fund was cut to $1. It affects the state budget and the fund that serves as a reserve for emergencies or budget shortfalls.

HI-2026-SB2964.title: RELATING TO PROPERTY INSURANCE.
HI-2026-SB2964.summary: Requires homeowners insurance producers to notify policyholders that they may submit information regarding improvements made to the insured residential property, which shall then be submitted to the homeowners insurer. Requires homeowners insurers to reevaluate the replacement cost estimate based on the information submitted by a policyholder, and offer the policyholder the option to purchase additional coverage to cover the full amount of the replacement cost estimate. Establishes administrative penalties for violations. Effective 1/1/2027. (CD1)

HI-2026-SB2043.title: RELATING TO INSURANCE.
HI-2026-SB2043.summary: Until 12/31/2031, specifies that captive insurance companies that are not risk retention captive insurance companies are subject to examination no later than five years after licensure and any additional examination at the discretion of the Insurance Commissioner. On or after 1/1/2032, subjects captive insurance companies that are not risk retention captive insurance companies to examination at least once every five years. Requires the Insurance Commissioner to submit a report to the Legislature before the Regular Session of 2031. Effective 7/1/2026. (CD1)

HI-2026-SB2043.aiSummary: The law changes how often certain captive insurance companies are checked by the Insurance Commissioner. Before 12/31/2031, they must be examined no later than five years after licensing, and the commissioner may do more exams if needed. Starting on 1/1/2032, they must be examined at least once every five years, and the commissioner must send a report to the Legislature before the 2031 Regular Session. Effective 7/1/2026.

Appropriates funds for the pilot program. Pilot program sunsets 6/30/2027. (CD1)

HI-2026-SB3132.aiSummary: Hospitals in Hawaii with emergency departments would have to send syndromic surveillance data, which is health data used to spot disease patterns, to the Department of Health. The department could set up a statewide system to collect and report that data. It became law as Act 222 in 2026.

HI-2026-GM1333.aiSummary: The law lets licensed mental health counselors be appointed as child custody evaluators in Hawaii. These evaluators help family courts decide custody cases, and the change affects families going through those cases and the professionals who can do the work. It took effect when the governor approved it on July 10, 2026.

HI-2026-GM1324.aiSummary: Signed into law, this measure requires all licensed hospitals with emergency departments to report de-identified syndromic surveillance data to the state health department. That data can include chief complaints, diagnoses, visit dates, patient demographics, ZIP code, and facility location. The health department may also set up a state reporting system and add more reporting rules for other entities.
